subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

On the ball

options.text: Sceptic of changes or developments and thoughtful to react them
Aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments but avoid to react to them
Unaware of any changes or developments and lazy to react to them

solution:
The correct answer is **option (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The phrase** "on the ball"** is an idiomatic expression in English. 
 
• It means **to be alert, attentive, knowledgeable; and quick to understand and react to a situation. (**किसी भी परिवर्तन या विकास से अवगत रहें और उन पर त्वरित प्रतिक्रिया दें**)**
 
 
• **For example:** if a person solves a problem at work very quickly, a colleague may say - "You're really **on the ball** today!"
 
 
 
• Hence, **"on the ball"** means to be aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them.
 
• Only option (2) suggests the exact meaning of the given idiom.

Therefore, the correct answer is **“Aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them”.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• We can remember this idiom in this way. A batsman always keeps his eye on the ball.
